I called a waitress over and asked for the bill, but she just waved her hand at me as if to say she was off duty, even though she was just sitting there on her phone. So professional!
Total lack of professionalism. I DO NOT RECOMMEND IT.

I had a lovely experience at L’ETO Soho during brunch. The atmosphere was vibrant and stylish, making it a great place to relax and enjoy coffee and dessert. I ordered a coffee and the caramel toffee cake. The coffee was excellent—rich, smooth, and perfectly made. The cake was beautifully presented and fresh, although I personally found it a little too sweet for my taste.

Overall, the quality of the food, coffee, and ambience was excellent. I would definitely visit again and try more of their famous cakes and brunch options.

Absolutely recommend.

text.text:
What a gem. I arrived just after 9am and was greeted by the loveliest staff, who made me feel welcome from the moment I walked in.

I picked up some Santos and Algerian Special beans and received excellent service from the lady who helped me. Friendly, knowledgeable, and genuinely passionate about coffee.

The shop itself is wonderful. It feels authentic, steeped in history, and full of character. In a city where so many places feel interchangeable, this feels like a true community institution. You can sense the heritage the moment you walk through the door.

It’s no wonder they have such fantastic reviews. I’m so glad London’s oldest coffee shop is still going strong after more than a century. Places like this are rare and deserve to be treasured.

When I learned that there was a coffee shop just off the beaten path in Soho that just so happens to share the name with my absolute favorite coffee drink I had to check it out.

I arrived 10min before close, so, I wasn't able to really sit in the ambiance that is Flat White. That being said, the staff was friendly, and the service was quick.

Before I talk about the drink experience, some additional details... I fell in love with flat whites when I visited Australia several years ago and I've been ordering and making them at home ever since. One thing worth noting is that a UK (and much of Europe) flat white is not quite the same as an Aussie or American flat white. It's still the same components; rich and bold espresso shot(s) accompanied by textured milk (steam milk infused with air to create a velvety texture), but in the UK they are restricted to cup sizes for some reason (mostly to do with the ratio of espresso to cup size). I was presented with a 4oz to-go coffee cup. The flavor was great, and with execution solid.

While this particular drink was delicious, I think I still prefer an Aussie flat white (or American). Having the barely bigger than espresso size feels like the drink is condensed while I want to enjoy the drink and flavor for longer.

text.text:
Overhyped, Impressive Presentation, Mediocre Flavours

I visited this establishment after seeing numerous visually appealing reels and photographs on social media. Like many others, I was drawn by its attractive aesthetic.
We ordered three items, all of which were rather average. The presentation and plating were excellent and visually striking, yet the taste fell short of the expectations created by its online popularity. The cakes were ordinary; I have had noticeably better versions from standard UK store bought cakes. The Triple Chocolate Mocha was similarly unremarkable and could easily be made at home.

Items Ordered:
1.  Triple Chocolate Mocha
2.  Double Chocolate Cake with Triple Chocolate Topping
3.  Croissants with Tomato, Cheese, and Basil

Total Bill: £26–30

It was notable that customers at the neighbouring tables also left significant portions of their orders unfinished. In addition, the seating felt quite cramped, with tables placed very close together, making movement difficult and blurring the lines between separate tables.

Conclusion:
I would not recommend this venue and would not return. It may appeal to those primarily interested in attractive surroundings for photographs, but it does not deliver a satisfying experience for those seeking quality food and comfortable dining.

Made a comeback to this café after two whole years! It’s such a famous spot that during my last visit, even though there wasn’t a queue, the terrace was completely packed, so I had to take my order to a nearby park. I still vividly remember how beautifully they packaged everything back then, which left such a wonderful impression that I just had to return!

This time, I visited on a Saturday afternoon. The staff took our order downstairs (you pay on your way out!), and we were guided to the upper floor, where we managed to snag a table. The table turnover is surprisingly quick, so people come and go pretty fast. We ordered an English Breakfast tea, scones, and a strawberry cheesecake. The scones were, as expected, absolutely legendary! Having a proper cream tea after such a long time was pure bliss. Another huge plus is that if you need more hot water or milk for your tea, you can just ask the staff, and they’ll top it up right away—we actually asked for a milk refill once. The secret to a perfect scone is the harmony between the clotted cream and strawberry jam, and their clotted cream is incredibly rich and delicious.

But the real hidden gem of the day was the almond croissant we ordered on a whim. Apparently, it’s a low-key favorite here! It was quite big, and the nutty flavor of the almonds paired perfectly with the flaky, crispy pastry. Next time I come back, ordering the scone and the almond croissant together is a non-negotiable. Plus, the atmosphere is so cozy and it’s a fantastic place for a proper catch-up. Such a satisfying visit! ☕️🧁✨

editorialSummary.text: Cozy bake shop for hefty housemade cookies in classic & unique flavors, plus soft-serve ice cream.

text.text:
If you love cookies and ice cream, then Crème is definitely worth visiting. The cookies here are genuinely some of the best I’ve had in London. They’re thick, soft in the centre, slightly crisp on the outside, and served warm.

The milk chocolate cookie is clearly the bestseller for a reason, but they also have great flavours like white chocolate miso, banana dark chocolate, vegan double chocolate, and dark chocolate.

The soft serve ice cream portions are generous and actually worth the price, which is becoming rare in London dessert spots. Combining the cookies with the ice cream is probably the best way to enjoy it.

The shop itself has a cool Soho dessert spot feel to it. Small, busy, and clearly popular. Definitely somewhere worth trying if you want a proper dessert stop rather than just another average cookie place.

I visited Onsu with a friend after seeing it on Instagram, and it certainly looks as stylish as it does online. The décor is modern and well presented, which is what attracted us in the first place. The only downside to the space is that it's quite small, and the tables are very close together, making it feel a little cramped.

We also ordered the tikka chicken masala, which was so spicy that it was almost impossible to eat, even for someone who normally enjoys spicy food. The heat completely overpowered the other flavours.

Overall, Onsu is a lovely café for its atmosphere and outstanding drinks, but based on our experience, the food didn't live up to the expectations. I'd happily return for the iced drinks, but I'd probably skip the food next time.

Onsu is easily one of the best bakeries in London. Their bread and cake deserve that title — especially the curry bun, which is absolutely outstanding and full of flavour. The other pastries and the salted egg yolk cake are also incredibly good.

The café is thoughtfully split into two sections: one for cakes and one for bread. Everything is freshly baked daily, which already puts them ahead of many places. We ordered from the pastries, and to our surprise, they reheated each item separately before serving. That level of care and attention to detail really stood out and made the experience even better.

We also tried their signature milk tea and dirty coffee — served in a cup frozen to -86°C before the Hong Kong-style milk tea is poured in. The presentation alone is impressive, but it’s not just a gimmick — the chilled cup actually enhances the texture, making the tea richer and smoother. It was delicious.

There are so many options on the menu, and honestly, everything looks worth trying. Definitely a café I’d highly recommend and will be coming back to.

You’d expect same-day freshness, especially on a busy weekend, although the shop was a ghost town so I wouldn’t be surprised if nothing was fresh.

Massively disappointing experience and awful cupcakes. Lola’s Cupcakes has never let me down, but Hummingbird absolutely has. I can only imagine their days are numbered if this is the standard they’re offering.

Would not recommend. Stay away.

They were very good. The best cookies I've had in London so far. My personal preference is a bit fluffier, but these are pretty flawless. I did find the triple chocolate a bit too sweet. But again, that's just me. The chocolate chip was very well balanced.

We did not need the chocolate dip, they were perfectly fine. My friend took one home, reheated it and said it was even better warm.

I'm not sure why they are a 4.2? But, I guess I've only tried the cookies. I would certainly order again and recommend trying it for yourself. I'm usually skeptical if Google reviews are below a 4.4, but, seeing the reel on Instagram gave me faith.

**Update** we also had them in, they were incredible. I've not had a better cookie in London.

text.text:
If you are a true coffee connoisseur, this Japanese specialty coffee shop is a dream come true. Unlike many places that try to do everything, this cafe focuses strictly on the art of coffee, and the results are extraordinary.
I tried their V60 pour-over using a light-roast Japanese bean, and the clarity of flavor was mind-blowing. The precision the baristas use—from the water temperature to the pouring technique—is a testament to the Japanese dedication to perfection. It’s not just a caffeine fix; it’s a craft.
The space itself is minimalist and serene, designed to let you focus entirely on the aroma and taste of your brew. No distractions, just high-quality beans and expert preparation. It’s easily one of the best spots in London for anyone who appreciates the subtle notes of a well-brewed cup.
The staff are incredibly knowledgeable and passionate about their craft. If you take your coffee seriously, you need to visit this place. A truly refined and authentic experience!

I have passed this place many times and been put off by the huge queues.

On a bank holiday, I took the chance to try it as it seemed quiet. However it turned out to be quite stressful on a hot sunny day.
As soon as you walk inside there is a till but no one was there to seve.
The kitchen looked busy and full of staff.
Then as you look to your left that is the rest of the shop, a small area to wait/collect your drink, which has the shop glass front on one side and the counter and kitchen the other. As it was a hot day, it was hot inside and then people came in to wait and collect the drinks.

There are qr codes for you to download the app to order your drinks. This really isn't great when the network  keeps dropping though.

Much later I found out I was charged 20p for a paper bag which I did not need or want.

The app is good to let you know where it is in the queue and to let u know when it is waiting to be collected.
I don't believe they called out my name or number, therefore I had to collect it myself, waving down a staff member.  She was friendly and gave me my drinks.

The mangoes inside the drinks were stringy, I had to spit these out. They were not made with care.
The cups are nice and solid but seems wasteful.
It was also probably the most expensive teas we have had

Overall for us, we did not enjoy the experience of ordering and the carelessness with the mangoes, it was not worth it.

I was a regular customer at this restaurant when it was Shack Fuyu and always enjoyed the food and great customer service. They have now relaunched as another location for their Bone Daddies chain. I was pleased to find the food and service is as good as ever.

I started off with the Chashu Pork and Katsu Chicken Bao Buns which were both delicious. The buns were well cooked and not too soft. Most importantly, the fillings had lots of flavour and although I enjoyed both, the Katsu Chicken was my favourite.

I then had the Spicy Miso Tonkotsu Ramen, as I like my noodles to have some heat and spice. I used to live in Japan and ramen was one of my favourite dishes. I thoroughly enjoyed the Bone Daddies' take on it. All of the ingredients were cooked well and the sauce was delicious. I could really taste the pork broth and the miso.

The good news is Shack Fuyu's famous Kinako French Toast is now available at Bone Daddies and I recommend leaving some room for it. It really is one of my favourite Japanese influenced desserts in London.

The other good news is the same lovely team are working at this new Bone Daddies and the customer service is up to the same high standard. All of the staff are friendly and helpful and the dishes I ordered were served quickly with no issues.

There are many ramen restaurants in London but I highly recommend giving Bone Daddies a visit. I will definitely continue to be a regular customer to satisfy my craving for ramen.

Overall, it was a total waste of money, and I regret choosing this place. For £13, I expected something enjoyable, but instead I got two cups of flavoured water. Definitely not recommended.

I’ve been a customer of Kissaten since it first opened inside the laundromat. Over the years, I’ve watched it grow in popularity, but unfortunately, the quality of service has declined. Today was the first time I left genuinely frustrated.

The shop is now overcrowded with gacha machines, leaving very little space to stand or move comfortably. A single small service window now handles both gacha and drink orders, resulting in long delays—especially when someone places a large gacha order. During my visit, around ten drink orders appeared to be stalled with no visible progress. Several customers voiced their concerns, but the staff seemed largely indifferent.

After waiting for about 15 minutes, we were informed that our drink was unavailable—something that should have been communicated at the time of ordering. No apology or compensation was offered. When we asked for a refund and expressed our frustration, the staff member told us we were “holding her up.” We weren’t given any proof of refund, only a verbal confirmation.

It’s disappointing to see a place I once really enjoyed become so poorly managed. What used to feel welcoming and efficient now feels disorganised and dismissive toward customers.

As for the gachapon machines, they feel questionable at best. My sister visited a few months ago and received the exact same keychain twice in a row—of the least popular character. Recently, I spent £6 on a broken Sanrio toy that didn’t even light up as advertised. It’s hard not to feel that the odds or quality aren’t quite as they should be.

The boba itself is decent but nothing special—certainly not enough to justify the experience or the prices.

Overall, Kissaten remains a cute and aesthetic stop in Soho, but at this point, it’s more style than substance. Sadly, it’s no longer worth the money or the frustration.
